5. Finite transport exposes the central electrochemical problem
Liquid flow

The liquid flows between the tall ribs; it is not forced entirely through the closing 3 µm tip gap.

The nominal clean channels are approximately:

5.5 µm wide.
43 µm high.
1.8 mm long.
Supplied in parallel at 30 mL/min total.

Using an introduced viscosity of 1.2 mPa·s gives approximately 144 kPa pressure loss including a manifold allowance. Hydraulic work is only about 0.072 W, but the model pays 1.5 W electrical pump input.

At 50% channel blockage, calculated pressure rises to approximately 268 kPa, exceeding the proposed 175 kPa rejection limit. Finite channels therefore cannot be treated as permanently clean, freely permeable paths.

7. Complete energy ledger

The following is the favorable 25°C bookkeeping case, before correcting the ionic-resistance inconsistency.

Duty	J per attempted cycle
Terminal electricity, conversion and stock-recovery leg	72.7
Liquid pumping	191.6
Controller and sensors	130.0
Dedicated proof and unloading actuation	180.0
Valves, drying air and water treatment	81.0
Removal of added rinse water	648.6
Micro-pan warm-up, heat loss, demisting and thermal reset	170.0
Allocated monitoring for the ten long research holds	17.3
Total per attempt	1,491.2
Per potential accepted service at 4% rejection	1,553.4

Even zero rejected attempts would not meet 1 kJ.

The 20 µL rinse sensitivity falls to approximately 0.945 kJ, but fails the cleanliness screen unless liquid holdup is also reduced tenfold.

The physically occupied robot share adds approximately 34.4 kJ per potential accepted service, bringing robot-plus-module operation to approximately 35.93 kJ. This broader allocation is reported separately; the module/cart already fails its own target.

Manufacturing is assigned an explicit, unverified 10 kWh per receiver pair, with at least a 1–30 kWh sensitivity range until vendor measurements exist. At 500 accepted services, the central allocation is 72 kJ/service. It is disclosed separately and not billed financially a second time inside purchased component prices.

The full ambient range can worsen the result. For example, cooling a 0.36 kg steel assembly from 40 to 35°C removes roughly 0.9 kJ of heat. At introduced cooling COP 0.5, that alone adds about 1.8 kJ electricity. The reference ledger does not claim free hot-end conditioning.
